sentence: Torricelli, 1644: the same air held a column of mercury about 76 cm high.
claim: Torricelli's mercury column (1644) stood about 76 cm above the dish, held by atmospheric pressure.
source_title: APS News, This Month in Physics History: Torricelli demonstrates the existence of a vacuum (October 2012)
note: End-card footnote (on screen, not spoken). Excerpt: 'The mercury settled at about 76 cm above the dish', attributed to atmospheric pressure. The Florence history-of-science museum's page (https://imss.fi.it/vuoto/eesper2.html) also dates it to spring 1644 at about 76 cm. NOAA's 29.92 inHg (760 mm) is the same column at standard pressure.
